column2: CASES IN WHICH COMPANY MAY BE WOUND UP BY THE COURT
A company may be wound up by the court, if—
the company has by special resolution resolved that
the company be wound up by the court;
the company does not commence its business within
a year from its incorporation or suspends it business
if  the  number  of  the  members  falls  below  the
minimum number required under subsection (2) of
the company is unable to pay its debts; or
the court is of opinion that it is just and equitable
that the company should be wound up.
